finding: Schizophrenia is described as a heritable, complex, multidimensional syndrome with psychotic, negative, cognitive, mood and motor manifestations and variable course.
~300 common and >20 rare variants implicate highly polygenic, mechanistically complex risk rather than a small set of discrete genetic diseases.
TRS requires persistent symptoms despite at least two adequate antipsychotic trials with adherence assessment; historical definitions varied markedly.
21% met a treatment-based TRS proxy; baseline factors predicted later TRS but the endpoint depended on treatment pathway/proxy definition.
12 prospective first-episode studies; younger age at onset was the most consistent predictor, but no decisive pretreatment classifier.
Early treatment resistance occurs in first-episode psychosis, supporting a subgroup that can emerge early rather than only after chronic illness.
TRS biomarker studies show heterogeneity in definitions and samples; heritability and inflammatory signals are promising but no validated pretreatment biomarker exists.
TRS showed lower/normal striatal dopamine synthesis than responders, suggesting possible non-hyperdopaminergic biology in a subset.
Clozapine-treated prior nonresponders had lower dopamine synthesis than first-line responders despite symptom matching; small sample.
TRS dopamine mechanisms are heterogeneous; low/normal presynaptic dopamine is one proposed route among multiple D2-related mechanisms.
Polygenic risk for TRS was associated with dopamine-system variation in healthy individuals, supporting biological liability but not a discrete disease boundary.
TRS polygenic risk maps to biological pathways but remains polygenic and requires external/clinical validation.
Immune-cell patterns differed across antipsychotic-responsive, clozapine-responsive and clozapine-resistant groups; cross-sectional response stratification.
Inflammatory proteins classified responsive/clozapine-responsive/clozapine-resistant groups with internal cross-validation; no external prospective validation.
Glutamate/GABA/NAA findings suggest biological differences in TRS and clozapine response but are heterogeneous and not a stable classifier.
Clozapine's unique efficacy may involve muscarinic, glutamatergic, immune and other mechanisms; mechanism remains unresolved.
Three psychosis Biotypes based on cognition, oculomotor and EEG/ERP measures replicated across large samples with high biomarker and temporal stability.
B-SNIP Biotypes showed stronger amygdala/hippocampal differences than DSM diagnoses, providing external neuroanatomical validation.
Clinical features predicted psychosis Biotypes with reasonable accuracy, supporting operationalization but not treatment utility.
Three Biotypes were stable in >1000 cases and relatives shared parts of biomarker patterns, supporting familial biological validity.
Conventional psychosis diagnoses showed continua, whereas transdiagnostic Biotypes had external validation; biological structure crossed DSM boundaries.
General plus positive, negative, disorganized, manic and depressive dimensions fit psychosis better and predicted Biotypes beyond DSM categories.
Normal, intermediate and impaired cognitive clusters were identified; siblings were enriched in intermediate cluster and brain-volume differences tracked cluster membership.
High- and low-cognition schizophrenia profiles were classified across discovery and independent validation samples (AUC ~0.76/0.73).
Negative symptom/social-cognition clusters reproduced across independent samples, supporting phenotypic structure but not distinct disease ontology.
Deficit syndrome/primary enduring negative symptoms occurred in roughly one-third across included cohorts; proposed as relatively homogeneous subgroup.
DMN topology/connectivity abnormalities replicated and correlated with avolition/apathy, supporting a dimensional neural correlate of negative symptoms.
No macroscale neuroimaging subtype profile was consistently reproduced; reported subtypes may reflect continuous variation.
Genetic liabilities associated differentially with symptom/cognitive dimensions, supporting quantitative heterogeneity rather than simple subtypes.
Paranoid/disorganized/catatonic etc. were removed because of poor stability, reliability and validity.
CBTp and some psychosocial interventions reduce symptoms in TRS, showing clinical treatment pathway differences without implying one biology.
Clozapine remains the evidence-based treatment for TRS, but delays in use are common and can affect outcome.
